card.statement:
Let $A\in{\mathbb C}^{\,n\times n}$ and let $\cal D$ be a $(0,\!*)$ matrix of size $n\times n$. The following three statements are equivalent:

- [(i)] The deformation $A+{\cal D}(\vec
      {\varepsilon})$ of $A\ ($see <<ref:a2z>>$)$ is miniversal.

- [(ii)] The vector space ${\mathbb C}^{\,n\times n}$ decomposes into the direct sum

\begin{equation*}
{\mathbb C}^{\,n\times
n}=T(A)
\oplus {\cal
D}({\mathbb C})
\end{equation*}

in which $T(A)$ and ${\cal
D}({\mathbb C})$ are defined in <<ref:eelie>> and <<ref:a2z>>.

- [(iii)] Each affine subspace of ${\mathbb
      C}^{\,n\times n}$ parallel to $T(A)$ intersects ${\cal
      D}(\mathbb C)$ at exactly one point.
card.label: Lemma 2.1

paper.title: Miniversal deformations of matrices of bilinear forms
paper.abstract: V.I. Arnold [Russian Math. Surveys 26 (2) (1971) 29-43] constructed a miniversal deformation of matrices under similarity; that is, a simple normal form to which not only a given square matrix A but all matrices B close to it can be reduced by similarity transformations that smoothly depend on the entries of B. We construct a miniversal deformation of matrices under congruence.

dependents.label: Corollary 1
